title: IT Support Engineer (Desktop Support)
summary: IT support engineers keep staff laptops, accounts, email and office networks working, and fix problems raised through a ticket queue or at the desk. They sit in the IT service desk or end-user computing team and pass harder issues to server, network or security teams.
dailyDuties: Pick up and close tickets in the service desk queue within SLA
Fix laptop, desktop and printer problems for staff
Reset passwords and manage user accounts in Active Directory
Set up mailboxes, Teams and OneDrive for new joiners
Prepare and hand over laptops for onboarding and collect them at exit
Troubleshoot Wi-Fi, LAN and VPN connection issues
Escalate unresolved issues to L2 or L3 teams with clear notes

skills.expectation: Fix laptop, desktop, printer and operating system problems for staff
Create users, reset passwords and manage groups in Active Directory or Entra ID
Set up mailboxes, Teams and OneDrive in Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace
Troubleshoot Wi-Fi, LAN, VPN, DNS and DHCP issues on user devices
Log, update and close tickets within SLA in a service desk tool such as ServiceNow
Explain fixes clearly to non-technical staff in person, on calls and in tickets
Work through a fault step by step and escalate to L2 or L3 with clear notes
Enrol and patch devices with Intune, SCCM or Jamf
Apply group policies and handle basic server tasks
Automate routine account and device tasks
Check antivirus or EDR alerts on user machines
Support users on Citrix or VMware virtual desktops

certifications.why: Proves the networking basics used daily in desktop support
Useful for support engineers moving towards network roles
